main_body: Large wooden crate (upper-left) with a second smaller crate overlapping at the lower right; both show a plank-striped tan lid above a dark brown front face with a diagonal brace
top_band: Tan plank-striped lid from rows ~1-8 (light and mid tan alternating rows), ending at a dark step at row 9
evidence: In a column through the middle of the large crate, rows 1-8 are a wide lighter tan lid with horizontal plank bands. Row 9 is an abrupt dark-brown step that works as the front edge and eave shadow. Rows 10-19 are the darker brown front face with a diagonal brace and a dark base. The top is several rows tall and clearly separate from the front, so it reads as a 3/4 crate. The brace is painted flat rather than inset, but the top and front are both clearly drawn.

style.evidence: The outline is dark brown and tinted to the wood, which matches the reference. The lid has about 3-4 tan tones but is built from plain horizontal stripes with no grain dots or knots. The front face is a large, nearly flat dark brown area with only a one-pixel diagonal brace and no wood grain, nails or per-plank highlights. Most tiles carry about 3-5 colours. That is thinner than the reference stall and well, which have many material ramps and texture dots, so it would look flatter next to them.
